about: Sourced life stories for the sons of Jacob and the two sons of Joseph. Written from Scripture (the site's KJV); there is no reviewed dossier for these people.

joseph-gen-30-24.short: Rachel's first son, sold by his brothers into Egypt, who rose from prison to rule Egypt under Pharaoh and kept his family alive through the famine.

paragraphs.text: Joseph was the first son of Rachel, who had been barren while her sister Leah bore sons; at his birth she said, "The LORD shall add to me another son." At seventeen he was feeding the flock with his brothers, and he "brought unto his father their evil report". Israel loved him more than all his children, "because he was the son of his old age", and made him a coat of many colours, and his brothers hated him. He dreamed that their sheaves bowed down to his sheaf, and that "the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me"; his father rebuked him, "but his father observed the saying."

Sent to see how his brothers were, Joseph found them at Dothan, and they plotted to kill "this dreamer"; Reuben persuaded them to put him in a pit instead, meaning to bring him back to his father. Judah then said, "let us sell him to the Ishmeelites", and Genesis goes on: "Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver". The brothers dipped his coat in a kid's blood and sent it to Jacob, who said, "an evil beast hath devoured him", and would not be comforted. Genesis says that "the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar", and later that Potiphar bought him "of the hands of the Ishmeelites".

In Egypt "the LORD was with Joseph", and Potiphar, captain of Pharaoh's guard, put all that he had into his hand. Potiphar's wife spoke to him day by day, asking him to lie with her, and he refused: "how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?" When she caught him by his garment, he left it in her hand and fled, and she accused him to the men of her house and to her husband. Potiphar put him in the prison where the king's prisoners were bound, and there the keeper of the prison committed all the prisoners to Joseph's hand. A psalm says of him, "Whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron".

In the prison he heard the dreams of Pharaoh's chief butler and chief baker, asking them, "Do not interpretations belong to God?" On the third day the butler was restored and the baker hanged, as Joseph had said, but the butler forgot Joseph. Two full years later Pharaoh dreamed of seven fat kine eaten up by seven lean kine, and seven good ears devoured by seven thin ears, and none of his magicians or wise men could interpret it. Brought hastily out of the dungeon, Joseph said, "It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace", and told him the dreams meant seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine.

Pharaoh set Joseph "over all the land of Egypt", put his own ring on Joseph's hand, called him Zaphnath-paaneah, and gave him Asenath, the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On, as his wife. Joseph was thirty years old. Through the seven years of plenty he laid up corn in the cities "as the sand of the sea", and before the famine came Asenath bore him two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim. When the famine came, "all countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy corn".

Ten of his brothers came down to buy corn and bowed before him with their faces to the earth; "Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him." He called them spies, kept Simeon bound, and sent the rest home with their money in their sacks, telling them to bring their youngest brother. When they came back with Benjamin, Joseph had his silver cup put in Benjamin's sack, and Judah offered to stay as a bondman "instead of the lad". Then Joseph sent every man out and said to his brothers, "I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt", and told them, "God did send me before you to preserve life."

Joseph sent wagons for his father, went up to meet him in Goshen, and "fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while." He gave his family a possession in the best of the land, as Pharaoh commanded, and fed them with bread. As the famine went on, he took the Egyptians' money, then their cattle, then their land for Pharaoh, and made it a law that Pharaoh should have the fifth part. Before he died, Jacob made Joseph swear to bury him with his fathers, took Joseph's two sons as his own, and said, "Joseph is a fruitful bough". Joseph wept over his father, had him embalmed, and went up with a very great company to bury him in Canaan.

After Jacob died, his brothers feared that Joseph would repay them, and sent asking him to forgive them. Joseph wept, and said, "Fear not: for am I in the place of God?" and "ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good". He lived a hundred and ten years, saw Ephraim's children of the third generation, and made the children of Israel swear to carry his bones up out of Egypt; he was embalmed and put in a coffin in Egypt. Moses took his bones with him, and they were buried at Shechem in the ground Jacob had bought, and Hebrews says that Joseph "gave commandment concerning his bones". Outside Genesis many verses on this record speak of "the children of Joseph" or "the house of Joseph", the two tribes descended from his sons.

judah-gen-29-35.short: Leah's fourth son, who proposed selling Joseph, had twin sons by Tamar, and offered himself as a bondman in Egypt in Benjamin's place.

paragraphs.text: Judah was the fourth son of Jacob and Leah. At his birth Leah said, "Now will I praise the LORD", and named him Judah. When his brothers plotted to kill Joseph, Judah said, "What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?" and proposed selling him to the Ishmeelites instead, "for he is our brother and our flesh."

Genesis then tells that Judah went down from his brothers and took the daughter of a Canaanite named Shuah, who bore him Er, Onan and Shelah. Er, whose wife was Tamar, "was wicked in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD slew him", and Onan, told to raise up seed for his brother, displeased the LORD, and the LORD slew him also. Judah sent Tamar to stay a widow in her father's house until Shelah was grown, but did not give her to Shelah.

Tamar covered herself with a veil and sat by the way to Timnath; Judah took her for a harlot and left his signet, bracelets and staff as a pledge. About three months later, told that she was with child, he said, "Bring her forth, and let her be burnt." She sent him the pledges, and Judah acknowledged them: "She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son." She bore twins, Pharez and Zarah.

When the famine drove the brothers back to Egypt, Judah told Jacob that they could not go without Benjamin, and said, "I will be surety for him". When the silver cup was found in Benjamin's sack, Judah and his brothers came back to Joseph's house, and Judah made a long plea, ending, "let thy servant abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren." It was then that Joseph made himself known to his brothers.

Jacob later sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph, to direct the way to Goshen. In his last words Jacob said, "Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise", called him "a lion's whelp", and said, "The sceptre shall not depart from Judah". Chronicles says that "Judah prevailed above his brethren, and of him came the chief ruler". Most verses on this record name the tribe, the kingdom or the land of Judah, or the Jews, rather than the man; Matthew and Luke (spelling him Judas and Juda) name Judah himself in the line of Jesus, and Hebrews says "our Lord sprang out of Juda".

levi-gen-29-34.short: Leah's third son, who with Simeon killed the men of Shechem; his daughter Jochebed was the mother of Aaron, Moses and Miriam.

paragraphs.text: Levi was the third son of Jacob and Leah, born after Reuben and Simeon. At his birth Leah said, "Now this time will my husband be joined unto me, because I have born him three sons", and so he was called Levi.

When Shechem the son of Hamor took Dinah, Levi's sister, and defiled her, Jacob's sons answered Shechem and his father "deceitfully", agreeing to marriages if every male of the city was circumcised. On the third day, while the men were sore, Simeon and Levi, "Dinah's brethren", took their swords and killed every male, Hamor and Shechem among them, and took Dinah out of Shechem's house. Jacob said to the two of them, "Ye have troubled me", and they answered, "Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?"

Levi went down to Egypt with his father and his sons Gershon, Kohath and Merari. In his last words Jacob spoke of Simeon and Levi together: "Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce", and "I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel." Exodus says that Levi lived a hundred and thirty-seven years.

Numbers names a daughter, Jochebed, "whom her mother bare to Levi in Egypt"; she married Amram, the son of Levi's son Kohath, and bore Aaron, Moses and Miriam. Exodus calls her Amram's "father's sister". Hebrews says that Levi "payed tithes in Abraham", for "he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." Most verses on this record name the tribe of Levi or the Levites, his descendants, rather than the man himself.

benjamin-gen-35-18.short: Jacob's youngest son, whose mother Rachel died giving birth to him; kept close by his father, and wept over by his brother Joseph in Egypt.

paragraphs.text: Benjamin was Rachel's second son and the youngest of Jacob's twelve. Rachel had hard labour on the way from Beth-el, a little way from Ephrath, and as she was dying she named him Ben-oni, "but his father called him Benjamin." She was buried in the way to Ephrath, "which is Beth-lehem", and Jacob set a pillar on her grave.

When famine came, Jacob sent ten of his sons to Egypt for corn but kept Benjamin back, "Lest peradventure mischief befall him." In Egypt Joseph demanded to see the youngest brother, and Jacob refused at first: "his brother is dead, and he is left alone". Only when Judah became surety for him did Jacob let him go: "If I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved."

In Egypt Joseph saw "his brother Benjamin, his mother's son", said, "God be gracious unto thee, my son", and went into his chamber to weep. At the meal Benjamin's portion was five times as much as any of the others'. Then Joseph had his silver cup put in Benjamin's sack, and when it was found there the brothers tore their clothes and went back to the city.

When Joseph made himself known, "he fell upon his brother Benjamin's neck, and wept; and Benjamin wept upon his neck." Joseph gave each brother changes of raiment, but gave Benjamin three hundred pieces of silver and five changes. Genesis names ten sons of Benjamin among those who went down to Egypt; the lists in Numbers and Chronicles name his sons differently.

In his last words Jacob said, "Benjamin shall ravin as a wolf: in the morning he shall devour the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil." Most verses on this record name the tribe of Benjamin rather than the man; Saul, the king Israel asked for, and the apostle Paul are both said to be of that tribe.

reuben-gen-29-32.short: Jacob's firstborn, by Leah, who tried to save Joseph from the pit but lost his birthright for lying with his father's concubine Bilhah.

paragraphs.text: Reuben was the firstborn of Jacob and Leah. Leah named him, saying, "Surely the LORD hath looked upon my affliction; now therefore my husband will love me." In the days of wheat harvest Reuben found mandrakes in the field and brought them to his mother, and Rachel asked Leah for them, offering that Jacob should lie with Leah that night.

Later, while Israel dwelt beyond the tower of Edar, "Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine: and Israel heard it." When the brothers plotted to kill Joseph, Reuben said, "Shed no blood", and had them put him in a pit, meaning to deliver him to his father again. He came back to find the pit empty, tore his clothes, and said, "The child is not; and I, whither shall I go?"

Later, in Egypt, when the brothers were taken for spies, Reuben said to the others, "Spake I not unto you, saying, Do not sin against the child; and ye would not hear?" At home, when Jacob would not let Benjamin go, Reuben said, "Slay my two sons, if I bring him not to thee", but Jacob refused. Reuben went down to Egypt with his sons Hanoch, Phallu, Hezron and Carmi.

In his last words Jacob called Reuben "my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength", but said, "Unstable as water, thou shalt not excel; because thou wentest up to thy father's bed". Chronicles says that because he defiled his father's bed "his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph". Most verses on this record name the tribe of Reuben, the Reubenites, rather than the man.

simeon-gen-29-33.short: Leah's second son, who with Levi killed the men of Shechem, and whom Joseph kept bound in Egypt until his brothers came back with Benjamin.

paragraphs.text: Simeon was the second son of Jacob and Leah, who said at his birth, "Because the LORD hath heard that I was hated, he hath therefore given me this son also". After Shechem the son of Hamor defiled their sister Dinah and the men of his city had been circumcised, Simeon and Levi took their swords, came upon the city, and killed every male, Hamor and Shechem among them. Jacob said to them, "Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land".

When the brothers first went down to Egypt for corn, Joseph took Simeon from them and "bound him before their eyes", keeping him while the rest went home to fetch Benjamin. Jacob said, "Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Benjamin away". When they came back with Benjamin, Joseph's steward brought Simeon out to them.

Genesis names Simeon's sons who went down to Egypt as Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and "Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman". Jacob's last words joined him with Levi: "Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations", and "I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel." Most verses on this record name the tribe of Simeon rather than the man.

gad-gen-30-11.short: Jacob's son by Zilpah, Leah's maid, named by Leah at his birth; Genesis tells almost nothing that he did himself.

paragraphs.text: Gad was the first son that Zilpah, Leah's maid, bore to Jacob; Leah had given Zilpah to Jacob as a wife when she saw that she had stopped bearing. Leah said, "A troop cometh", and named him Gad.

Genesis tells nothing that Gad did by name. It says that at seventeen Joseph fed the flock "with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah", Gad among them, and "brought unto his father their evil report". He was one of the ten brothers who went down to Egypt to buy corn, and later went down with Jacob's household; Genesis names his sons as Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi and Areli. Exodus says that "Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation."
In his last words Jacob said, "Gad, a troop shall overcome him: but he shall overcome at the last." Most verses on this record name the tribe of Gad, the Gadites, rather than the man.

asher-gen-30-13.short: Jacob's second son by Zilpah, Leah's maid, named by Leah for her happiness; Genesis tells almost nothing that he did himself.

paragraphs.text: Asher was the second son that Zilpah, Leah's maid, bore to Jacob. Leah named him, saying, "Happy am I, for the daughters will call me blessed".

Genesis tells nothing that Asher did by name. It says that at seventeen Joseph fed the flock "with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah", Asher among them, and "brought unto his father their evil report". He was one of the ten brothers who went down to Egypt to buy corn, and later went down with Jacob's household; Genesis names his sons as Jimnah, Ishuah, Isui and Beriah, with a daughter, "Serah their sister". Exodus says that "Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation."
In his last words Jacob said, "Out of Asher his bread shall be fat, and he shall yield royal dainties." Most verses on this record name the tribe of Asher rather than the man.

naphtali-gen-30-8.short: Jacob's second son by Bilhah, Rachel's maid, named by Rachel for her wrestlings with her sister; Genesis tells almost nothing that he did himself.

paragraphs.text: Naphtali was the second son that Bilhah, Rachel's maid, bore to Jacob; Rachel had given Bilhah to Jacob because she herself bore him no children. Rachel named him, saying, "With great wrestlings have I wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed".

Genesis tells nothing that Naphtali did by name. It says that at seventeen Joseph fed the flock "with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah", Naphtali among them, and "brought unto his father their evil report". He was one of the ten brothers who went down to Egypt to buy corn, and later went down with Jacob's household; Genesis names his sons as Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer and Shillem. Exodus says that "Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation."
In his last words Jacob said, "Naphtali is a hind let loose: he giveth goodly words." Most verses on this record name the tribe of Naphtali or its land, rather than the man.

zebulun-gen-30-20.short: The sixth and last son Leah bore to Jacob, named when she said her husband would now dwell with her; Genesis tells almost nothing he did.

paragraphs.text: Zebulun was the sixth and last son that Leah bore to Jacob, born after Issachar and before his sister Dinah. Leah named him, saying, "God hath endued me with a good dowry; now will my husband dwell with me, because I have born him six sons".

Genesis tells nothing that Zebulun did by name. Genesis says of Joseph's brothers, without naming them, that when they saw their father loved Joseph more than them all they "hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him." He was one of the ten brothers who went down to Egypt to buy corn, and later went down with Jacob's household; Genesis names his sons as Sered, Elon and Jahleel. Exodus says that "Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation."

In his last words Jacob said, "Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea; and he shall be for an haven of ships; and his border shall be unto Zidon." Most verses on this record name the tribe of Zebulun or its land, rather than the man.

issachar-gen-30-18.short: Leah's fifth son, born after she traded Reuben's mandrakes to Rachel and named for her hire; Genesis tells almost nothing he did himself.

paragraphs.text: Issachar was the fifth son of Jacob and Leah. In the days of wheat harvest Reuben brought his mother mandrakes, and when Rachel asked for some, she offered that Jacob should lie with Leah that night in return. Leah told Jacob, "I have hired thee with my son's mandrakes", and "God hearkened unto Leah, and she conceived". She named the child Issachar, saying, "God hath given me my hire, because I have given my maiden to my husband".

Genesis tells nothing that Issachar did by name. Genesis says of Joseph's brothers, without naming them, that when they saw their father loved Joseph more than them all they "hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him." He was one of the ten brothers who went down to Egypt to buy corn, and later went down with Jacob's household; Genesis names his sons as Tola, Phuvah, Job and Shimron. Exodus says that "Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation."

In his last words Jacob said, "Issachar is a strong ass couching down between two burdens", who "bowed his shoulder to bear, and became a servant unto tribute." Most verses on this record name the tribe of Issachar rather than the man.

ephraim-gen-41-52.short: Joseph's younger son, born in Egypt, on whom the dying Jacob laid his right hand, setting him before his elder brother Manasseh.

paragraphs.text: Ephraim was the second son of Joseph and Asenath, the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On, born in Egypt before the years of famine came. Joseph named him, saying, "For God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction."

When Jacob was sick, Joseph brought his two sons to him, and Jacob said, "thy two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh... are mine; as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine." Joseph set Manasseh, the firstborn, toward Jacob's right hand, but Jacob laid his right hand on Ephraim's head, the younger, and his left on Manasseh's, "guiding his hands wittingly". When Joseph tried to move it, Jacob said, "his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations", and "he set Ephraim before Manasseh."

Joseph lived to see Ephraim's children of the third generation. In its list of "the sons of Ephraim" Chronicles names Ezer and Elead, "whom the men of Gath that were born in that land slew, because they came down to take away their cattle", and says that "Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brethren came to comfort him." Afterwards his wife bore a son, and he named him Beriah, "because it went evil with his house."
Hebrews says that "By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph". Most verses on this record name the tribe or people of Ephraim rather than the man.

manasseh-gen-41-51.short: Joseph's firstborn, born in Egypt, on whom the dying Jacob laid his left hand, setting his younger brother Ephraim before him.

paragraphs.text: Manasseh was the firstborn of Joseph and Asenath, the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On, born in Egypt before the years of famine came. Joseph named him, saying, "God... hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father's house."

When Jacob was sick, Joseph brought Manasseh and Ephraim to him, and Jacob took them as his own, "as Reuben and Simeon". Joseph set Manasseh toward his father's right hand, but Jacob laid his right hand on the younger, Ephraim, and his left on Manasseh, "guiding his hands wittingly; for Manasseh was the firstborn." Joseph said, "Not so, my father: for this is the firstborn", and Jacob answered, "he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great: but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he".

Joseph lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, who "were brought up upon Joseph's knees." Chronicles names Manasseh's sons Ashriel, "whom she bare", and Machir, saying "his concubine the Aramitess bare Machir the father of Gilead". Joshua calls Manasseh "the firstborn of Joseph". Most verses on this record name the tribe of Manasseh, often "the half tribe of Manasseh", rather than the man.
